    if fy:

class TBlock(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, d, h, ff):
        super().__init__()
        self.h = h
        self.ln1 = nn.LayerNorm(d)
        self.qkv = nn.Linear(d, 3 * d)
        self.o = nn.Linear(d, d)
        self.ln2 = nn.LayerNorm(d)
        self.f1 = nn.Linear(d, ff)
        self.f2 = nn.Linear(ff, d)

    def forward(self, x):
        B, N, C = x.shape
        hd = C // self.h
        qkv = self.qkv(self.ln1(x)).reshape(B, N, 3, self.h, hd).permute(2, 0, 3, 1, 4)
        q = qkv[0]
        k = qkv[1]
        v = qkv[2]
        a = torch.softmax(torch.matmul(q, k.transpose(-2, -1)) / math.sqrt(hd), dim=-1)
        y = torch.matmul(a, v).transpose(1, 2).reshape(B, N, C)

        m = mask[:, :self.n_place].to(obs.dtype)
        pad = K * Y * X - self.n_place
        if pad > 0:
            m = F.pad(m, (0, pad))
        m = m.reshape(B, K, Y * X).transpose(1, 2)
        x = self.obs_emb(o) + self.mask_emb(m) + self.pos
        for b in self.blocks:
            x = b(x)
        x = self.lnf(x)
        place = self.pout(x).transpose(1, 2).reshape(B, -1)[:, :self.n_place]
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([x.mean(1), x.amax(1)], dim=1))
        logits = F.pad(place, (0, 1)) + F.pad(self.done_head(g), (self.n_place, 0)) + self.gall(g)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

analyses.2: All six round-1 nets scored 0 on dev and also had 0 training success. Two runs should have covered every flip or transpose of a type-major layout: set A with 8 obs symmetries (r1c3) and set B with 8 obs symmetries (r1c4). With all 8 obs views, any single layout can align obs and actions, yet both scored 0. That points away from a plain reorientation and towards a different action index order. The leading suspect is type-minor ordering, a=(y·X+x)·K+t, where t is the brick type. Read as type-major, it scrambles cells in a way no convolution can undo. A type-in-the-middle order (YKX) is less likely. Adding LayerNorm also failed with set A, with or without obs symmetries, so input scale alone is not the cause. Round 2 follows step 5: type-minor sets A and B, a YKX set, and the full combination (obs symmetries + LayerNorm + global context in each block + a dilated block) with type-major A and with type-minor A. Any nonzero score is the signal.
analyses.3: All 12 trials scored 0 on dev, and none built a single target in training. Ruled out: type-major layouts under every grid symmetry, since set A plus 8 obs views covers every orientation. Also ruled out: type-minor and type-middle readings, and LayerNorm for input scale, alone or combined with global context and a dilated block. The starting net ran without crashing, so n_place is the full n_types·Y·X. What remains is a scramble that a conv grid frame cannot express, in the actions, the mask or the obs (a roll, a permutation or a memory-order mismatch), or a reward/credit problem. Round 3 therefore tests nets that make no layout assumption. Two flat MLP policies read the whole obs and mask through Linear layers. Three hybrid conv nets add a learned Linear re-layout stem and a Linear placement head. One run follows the program's fallback: a separate critic with gamma 0.99 and ent 0.01. Any nonzero score is the signal.
analyses.4: All 18 trials scored 0 on dev, and none built a design exactly even in training. That includes sets A and B, obs symmetries, LayerNorm, type-minor and type-middle orders, the full combination, flat MLPs, Linear re-layout hybrids and a separate critic with gamma 0.99. So any grid symmetry between the obs and the actions is probably ruled out, and so are the K-ordering scrambles. Three untested index deviations could give exactly 0 for every net so far. (1) DONE comes first and every placement index is shifted by one, which conv nets cannot learn at row wrap-around; in that case the DONE logit is also wrong. (2) Placements use a compact index with only the anchors that fit, so n_place = Σ(Y−dy+1)(X−dx+1). (3) Cells are permuted arbitrarily, which needs attention with learned positions. Every candidate adds a Linear from global features to all action logits, so DONE can sit at any index. Single-layout versions avoid diluting the signal across a sum of layouts. This is the last round, so any nonzero score wins.
